reported_success.quote: more mixed valence in comparison with control songs according ... to MIN (Schimmack, 2001) but less mixed valence according to ... the Grifﬁn formula (Thompson et al., 1995).

notes: Identity verified independently: supplied text has matching title Unique Affective Profile of Music-Evoked Nostalgia: An Extension and Conceptual Replication of Barrett et al.’s (2010) Study, authors Sarah Hennessy, Timothy Greer, Shrikanth Narayanan, Assal Habibi, and DOI 10.1037/emo0001389. It is the primary research article (2024 advance online publication), with Methods, Results, Discussion, tables and references through printed p.23; not merely an abstract. No PDF was supplied. Original side and unassigned fields are placeholders only. The requested standardized beta is not established: context variables were raw and not standardized; person scores were mean-centered, not described as standardized. Printed β coefficients and Cohen’s f² candidates are retained without conversion. Two context-only mixedness tests are explicitly reported: Griffin β=−1.47, t(524)=−13.34, adjusted p<.001, f²=0.086; MIN β=0.26, t(522)=4.03, adjusted p<.001, f²=0.009 (p.5; Table 6 p.8). Description does not choose the mixedness formula. Outcomes are mixedness ratings with nostalgia/control condition predictor. Common candidate-model sample is explicitly N=582 participant clusters and 2,234 song observations. It is retained only as a candidate because row-to-test mapping is unresolved. Participants with improper responses (14) or no matched control songs (172) were excluded; unmatched song pairs were excluded. No N was inferred from df and no arithmetic sum was used.
